before: A room opened from a Word file wrote the normalized package and read it back, and loaded from those trees; a checkpoint of version 6 kept the written bytes as its base. Code that depends on the written form (attribute order, a text's xml:space, prefixes, the part bytes that seed a custom XML part's id) then gave the room other results than the editor alone, which reads the file as uploaded.
after: The room loads from the uploaded package as every open normalizes it, and a checkpoint keeps the uploaded bytes as its base. Every later open normalizes them to the same trees and node ids, so the live room, every reopen and the editor alone read one form of the file. The normalization validates only what it changed.
reason: Change messages, the change log and its kinds, the checkpoint layout and the Yjs document format do not change. Item addresses come from the same normalized trees as before the written base, and a checkpoint with a written base still opens: the normalization of written bytes changes nothing. A room admits only clients of its own code version, so every copy opens the file the same way. Migration: start fresh rooms; ordered rooms are not deployed yet.
